requests.reason: Inspect metadata discovery, Open validation and retention selection to determine whether reclamation consumes metadata eligibility as evidence of recoverability.
Inspect the Close-to-reclamation path and its error branches for protections establishing usable replacement snapshots before older snapshots are removed.

audit_question.question: When retention reclamation consumes file_snapshot_metadata_eligible, can an entry whose state fails Open validation displace an older readable snapshot, or does publication or reclamation establish a stronger replacement guarantee before deletion?
audit_question.importance: If retention removes readable recovery evidence while retaining unusable replacements, restart recovery could lose an available snapshot fallback. Whether this scenario is permitted and whether retained logs or other snapshots mitigate its consequence remain unresolved.
contexts: Listed snapshot with state that fails Open validation; reachability and fault applicability remain unestablished
counterevidence: The provisional inventory describes temporary-directory exclusion and finalized metadata before publication; these may prevent incomplete writes from entering retention selection.
The provisional inventory describes CRC validation in Open, which may reject unusable snapshots at recovery time but does not itself establish retention safety.
No attached source currently verifies these protections or their applicability.
unknowns: Whether retention validates state contents or relies solely on metadata eligibility.
Whether every relevant reclamation invocation follows successful publication of a readable replacement.
Which error or permitted interference scenarios can produce metadata-eligible entries that fail Open.
What recovery guarantees and storage fault assumptions apply to retention.
Whether recovery can use other snapshots or retained logs after the hypothesized deletion.
audit_question.trigger_rationale: The accepted inventory distinguishes metadata eligibility from successful state validation and identifies reclamation as a consumer of the weaker fact. This supports a focused cross-path comparison, but does not establish a defect or an applicable recovery obligation.

input.selection_rationale: Select consumption of file_snapshot_metadata_eligible. Discovery, validation and reclamation expose a bounded discriminator with potentially significant recovery consequences. First inspect the actual consumer and publication protections; no normative obligation is justified from inventory assertions alone.
